answer: One workable design: attribute weight by earnings history, so a new identity starts at nearly zero influence, because mesa only stays cheap while buying 1000 fresh accounts buys almost no vote weight until each one has real history. Concretely, vine is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any vertex approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
